refnamediv.refpurpose: Button-based control panel applet for signal routing systems

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: buttonpanel1 is a button-based control applet that can be used to control signal routing and GPIO devices via Drouter's ProtocolJ interface.

listitem.para: Display an ARM button in addition to the source buttons to enable two-click control.
Use cols button columns per row.
Insert a strip containing a title and one or more GPIO widgets. This option may be given multiple times.
The following widgets are available:
A widget that provides an audio/visual alert in response to a GPIO state.
A push button that sets the state of a single GPIO line.
A text label.
An indicator for a single GPIO line.
A "multi-state" indicator that shows the states of all five lines of a single GPIO channel simultaneously.
A separator (short vertical line) that can be used to set off various sections of a strip.
For a detailed description of the widget-spec for each type, see the WIDGET SPECIFICATIONS section, below.
Print a short usage message and then exit.
Use the Drouter server at host-name. Default value is localhost. See also the section ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES, below.
Display an enumerated list of available sound output devices.
Do not apply a maximum size limit to the top-level application window after calculating the widget layout. Useful only for debugging.
The number of the output to monitor and control. Optionally, the router number (default 1) may also be given. This option may be given multiple times.
Play the specified audio file, then exit.
Use the specified sound device for playing audio. (Use the --list-sound-devices for generating a list of available devices).
Print the version string and then exit.
These options do nothing, and exist solely for backwards compatibility.

refsect2.title: Alerts
refsect2.para: An alert widget provides an audio/visual alert in response to a GPIO state. It includes a push button that provides both a visual indication for the alerted state as well as the ability to acknowledge (silence) the associated audio alarm indication.
Alert widgets use a widget-spec as follows:
/alert:color:direction:router:endpoint:legend:mask:sound
color specifies the color of the acknowledgment button. The following colors are recognized:
direction specifies the direction of the specified signal, with i for GPI and o for GPO.
router is the number of the Software Authority router containing the specified GPIO, as given in the RouterNumbers command.
endpoint is the Software Authority input (for GPIs) or output (for GPOs) number of the specified GPIO, as given by the SourceNames or DestNames command respectively.
legend is the text to be associated with the acknowledgment button.

mask is a five letter specifier that indicates which line(s) of the specified GPIO are used to determine if the alert is in an active (alarming) state. The following characters can be used:
h
The specified line, in HIGH state.
l
The specified line, in LOW state.
x
The specified line has no effect with the alert.

sound is the name of an audio file whose contents will be looped (played) on the audio device specified by the --sound-device on the command line when the alert becomes active until either the acknowledgment button has been clicked or the alert has become inactive. The specified audio sample must reside in the /etc/drouter/sounds subdirectory, and be of type WAV or AIFF.

refsect2.title: Buttons and Lamps
refsect2.para: Button or lamp widgets use a widget-spec as follows:
/button:color:direction:router:endpoint:legend:mask /lamp:color:direction:router:endpoint:legend:mask
color specifies the color of the button or lamp. The following colors are recognized:
direction specifies the direction of the specified signal, with i for GPI and o for GPO.
router is the number of the Software Authority router containing the specified GPIO, as given in the RouterNumbers command.
endpoint is the Software Authority input (for GPIs) or output (for GPOs) number of the specified GPIO, as given by the SourceNames or DestNames command respectively.
legend is the text to be associated with the button or lamp.

mask is a five letter specifier that indicates which line(s) of the specified GPIO are connected to the button or lamp to indicate a ON state. The following characters can be used:
h
The specified line, in HIGH state.
l
The specified line, in LOW state.
x
The specified line has no effect with the control.

refsect2.title: Labels
refsect2.para: label widgets use a widget-spec as follows:
/label:legend
legend is the text to be associated with the button or lamp.

refsect2.title: Multistate Indicators
refsect2.para: Multistate indicator widgets use a widget-spec as follows:
/multi:direction:router:endpoint:legend
direction specifies the direction of the specified signal, with i for GPI and o for GPO.
router is the number of the Software Authority router containing the specified GPIO, as given in the RouterNumbers command.
endpoint is the Software Authority input (for GPIs) or output (for GPOs) number of the specified GPIO, as given by the SourceNames or DestNames command respectively.
legend is the text to be associated with the indicator.

refsect2.title: Separators
refsect2.para: sep widgets simply use a widget-spec as follows:
/sep

refsect1.title: Environmental Variables
refsect1.para: The following environmental variables can be used to influence the behavior of buttonpanel1:

listitem.para: If no --hostname option is given, buttonpanel1 will attempt to use the Drouter server referenced in $DROUTER_HOSTNAME. If $DROUTER_HOSTNAME is not defined, then the Drouter server at localhost will be used.

refsect1.title: Bugs
refsect1.para: The GTK windowing styles do not support overriding the background color of button elements (as is commonly done in Drouter panel widgets). This can be worked around by using the -style option to specify a different window style --e.g. -style plastique
